newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish Oct GDP growth bodes well for '97-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Finnish Oct GDP growth bodes well for '97-analysts.

text.p: A robust gross domestic product reading in October showed Finnish growth on track to accelerate in 1997 as forecast and confirmed the economy had been very strong in the final quarter, economists said on Tuesday.
GDP measured at the producer price level increased 5.7 percent year-on-year in October -- the quickest pace of growth since March 1995, Statistics Finland (SF) said.
"It confirms our view that 1997 growth will start with a four, it may even start with a five," said Petteri Hirvonen, economist at brokerage Davy Protos.
Merita Bank chief economist Juha Ahtola said the October figure showed that "there is certainly no reason to downgrade our 3.5 percent growth forecast for 1997."

"It will depend mainly on domestic demand and construction," he said, referring to next year's growth prospects. "The big question mark is construction, whether it will accelerate strongly," Ahtola added.
The economists agreed there was no reason to fear inflation would shoot higher soon despite the rapid growth.
"I don't think growth is yet so strong that inflation would pick up speed significantly," said Tarja Heinonen, economist at bank Postipankki.
The consumer price index is widely forecast to rise next year from its current levels below one percent, mainly as food prices and interest rates stop falling.

Hirvonen at Protos, which earlier in the autumn of 1996 called for a pre-emptive rate hike by the Bank of Finland to show it is serious about keeping inflation in check, now said inflation expectations could start increasing next year although actual CPI figures would remain moderate.
In November, CPI rose 0.7 percent year-on-year.

Ahtola said it was unlikely that core inflation -- a key monetary policy gauge monitored by the Bank of Finland -- would rise above one percent before the end of 1997 while the central bank has said it would come near two percent by end-1997.
Core inflation rose 0.3 percent year-on-year in October.
"The only category with any noticeable price rise pressures is housing, everywhere else we have oversupply and competition will see to it that prices don't rise," Ahtola said.
SF said October GDP growth rested on strong growth in all major categories of the economy.
"All central components increased equally, this is very stable growth," Ahtola said.
Fourth-quarter growth measured by market prices would be "very strong," Hirvonen said, putting the figure at 5-6 percent. This would bring 2.8-2.9 percent growth for the full year 1996, he said.
"Growth in the final quarter has been quite strong," agreed Heinonen at Postipankki. She put 1996 growth at 2.5-2.6 percent.
Ahtola said he expected final quarter growth in the region of 3-4 percent resulting in "at least" 2.5 percent 1996 GDP growth.
The trade and commerce component was unlikely to have been as strong in November and December as in October, he said.
SF is scheduled to release preliminary 1996 GDP data on February 13 while official Q4 and full-year figures are due for publication on March 21.
